main_body: Beehive thatched hut: a large conical straw roof with banded thatch rows over a short clay wall with an arched doorway
top_band: The roof is the top surface. At x=40 it runs from about row 2 to row 55 in banded straw tones (L 186/154/124/95), lightest at the upper left, down to the eave edge at about row 55. It reads as a sloped surface seen from above.
evidence: The thatch roof is a large foreshortened slope with per-row shadow lines, and its eave overhang casts a dark band onto the clay wall at about rows 56-60. The wall below is a separate vertical face of about 22 rows with a darker base strip. The doorway is inset, with a lintel/frame and a dark interior, and the arch cuts up into the thatch. No receding side face is drawn. It matches the Beodeul roof-over-wall construction, so it counts as a correct 3/4 building.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 6 lightness steps with per-row shadow lines and clumped highlights. The outline is dark brown (only 5% neutral edge pixels), matching the material tone. The wall has plank dashes and a gradient, and the foundation strip is speckled. Median 8 colours per tile is below the references (11 and 18), and the 31 distinct colours are well below their 66 and 185, but the 12% flat-fill coverage comes mostly from the dark door interior and is minor. Overall craft is acceptable next to the references, though a little thinner and more repetitive.
